_comment: Free-tier quotas and the endpoint allowlist, as data rather than as constants in code.
Story 3.2 AC5: these are configuration. INV-8: an endpoint absent from `endpoints` fails
configuration validation, which is what keeps a paid endpoint from ever being configured.
These numbers move. Re-verify at the start of each epic and update `verifiedOn`.
`fallbackBackoffMs` is used only when a 429 carries no timing header at all.
`maxBackoffMs` bounds how long one call may block the Harness. A daily quota
legitimately resets hours away, and sleeping that inside complete() would hang
a Match with no diagnostic. The signal still reports the provider's true
interval, so the runner can make the long decision that is its job (AD-9).
Story 3.3. Cerebras publishes rate limits per-account rather than a
static table (inference-docs.cerebras.ai/support/rate-limits, fetched
2026-08-01) -- 30 RPM / ~1,000 RPD / 60,000 TPM is the figure this
story measured against a real free-tier key. Re-verify at the start
of each epic; a materially different account would need this file
updated, not the adapter.
Story 3.3. Google AI Studio's console is the authoritative source of
current numbers (ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/rate-limits points
there rather than publishing a static table). RPM/RPD below are as
measured 2026-07-30; TPM is a conservative estimate pending
re-verification against the console -- flagged in deferred-work.md.
Two models, two endpoints: the model is part of the URL path for
this provider, so each is its own allowlist entry (INV-8).
